02 — RUN IT YOURSELF

A small Python example.
A real Pinocchio result.

Pinocchio + NumPy are enough.
MuJoCo and Jupyter are optional.

01

Get the example

The ZIP contains the script, G1 URDF, environment file and license. Keep the folder together.

Download minimal example ↓8 KB · Python + URDF02

Create the environment

Install Miniforge, or use Conda you already have. In the extracted folder, run the commands alongside.

Conda is the recommended route for mixed operating systems. The code is verified on Linux; Windows and macOS still need a classroom pilot.

Open Miniforge Prompt in the extracted g1-left-arm folder.

TERMINAL
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate g1-left-arm
python left_arm_ik.py
EXPECTED RESULTconverged: 9 updates;
position error 0.0687 mm

Try your own torso-frame target:
python left_arm_ik.py --target 0.30 0.25 0.10

Use the supplied Conda file. The pinned pin==3.9.0 pip release is Linux-only; do not mix the pip and Conda distributions.

OPTIONAL NEXT STEP

Put the result in MuJoCo.

The complete lab adds a full-robot viewer, a notebook and pose IK. Keep this page as your short implementation guide.

Three details to get right

Frame consistencyThe tool position, target and Jacobian must use the same axes.

Named joint mappingUse joint names and their indices, rather than copying array positions.

Honest stoppingA returned configuration is not enough. Check status and residual.
